conviction_note: The Q3 lines were largely pre-guided at the 29 Sep pre-close call and consensus already reflects that guidance (NFT 216 vs the guided lower half of 200-250, loan losses 75m vs 'closer to 10bp'). What is left is a small negative on capital return (no buyback since April; management prioritising growth) offset by a small positive on the Q4 NII tailwind from the ECB hikes. abs_move is 3.5, set from the European pre-released base plus Nordea's own Q3 prints (+6.3% in 2024 and +3.5% in 2025, both on buyback days). p_up is 52 because the evidence is balanced. The findings sum to -0.05 and the scaled number is +0.14; both are inside noise and they differ only by that rounding.

already_public.what: Pre-close analyst call. Higher policy rates support NII over time, but short-term headwinds come from funding costs and customer notice periods. Lending-margin pressure continued in Q3. The deposit hedge is a ~EUR 10m sequential headwind. NFT will be in the lower part of the 200-250m normal range. Costs slightly up q/q. Loan losses up toward the ~10bp long-term level. The stock fell ~1.1-1.5% that day while peers rose.

2026 outlook: ROE >15%, cost-to-income 44-45% (narrowed from ~45% at Q2), long-term loan loss ~10bp, management buffer 150bp over the CET1 requirement. CET1 15.7% (15.4% for regulatory reporting per ECB expectations). Mid-year dividend EUR 0.34 already paid. No new buyback announced at Q2.
Report date and time: Q3 2026 results on 15 Oct 2026 at about 07:30 EET, before the Helsinki open.

new_in_release.expect: Close to consensus. The pre-close call guided NFT, costs and loan losses. NII (consensus 1,805m, +1.5% q/q) is the one line not quantified, and the pre-close comments on lending-margin pressure and the hedge headwind make it lean slightly to the low side.

Capital return is the swing line. Nordea announced EUR 250m programmes with Q3 in both 2024 and 2025. No programme has been announced since the December 2025 one completed on 2026-04-21, and at Q2 management said it is prioritising capital for growth. Inderes models one more EUR 250m programme in 2026. Whether one comes, and its size, is genuinely uncertain; the lean is slightly negative.
ROE >15% and C/I 44-45% are expected to be reiterated (Inderes). Commentary on the Q4 NII uplift from the ECB's June and September hikes is likely positive. A formal guidance change is unlikely.
None. The mid-year dividend was decided in July.

findings.finding: At the 29 Sep pre-close call Nordea pre-guided the soft Q3 lines: NFT in the lower part of 200-250m, costs slightly up q/q, loan losses rising toward 10bp, continued lending-margin pressure and a ~EUR 10m deposit-hedge headwind. Consensus already reflects this (NFT 216m, LL 75m). The one residual is NII, where consensus at 1,805m (+1.5% q/q) sits slightly above what the 'short-term headwinds' language implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell ~1.1-1.5% on the pre-close day itself while peers rose. In Q3 2025 a loan-loss reversal drove a beat and the stock rose ~3.5% (estimated-date history).
findings.original_quote: Nordea sade också att det är rimligt att anta att press på utlåningsmarginalerna har fortsatt under tredje kvartalet. ... Nettot lär enligt banken därför bli lägre än vanligt i kvartalet, sannolikt i den nedre delen av det intervall på 200-250 miljoner euro (Nordea also said it is reasonable to assume lending-margin pressure continued in Q3 ... NFT likely in the lower part of the 200-250m range)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock dropped on the call, and consensus NFT and LL match the guidance. Only the unquantified NII residual is open. If the market had fully priced an NII shortfall, consensus would sit at or below Q2's 1,779m rather than at 1,805m.
findings.independence: Inderes's estimate is 1,800m NII, also with 'the effect of rate rises visible with a lag' (https://www.inderes.fi/analyst-comments/nordea-q326-ennakko-koronnostot-ovat-parantaneet-tulosnakymaa). Same direction, but it is an analyst reading the same call.

findings.finding: Capital return is uncertain at the slot where Nordea has announced buybacks two years running. No programme has been announced since the EUR 500m December-2025 programme completed on 2026-04-21. At Q2 management deferred distribution and prioritised growth capital (corporate lending +9%, LC&I +14%). CET1 is 15.7% (15.4% reported) against a 15.3% requirement-plus-buffer, and Inderes still models a EUR 250m programme in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024, an unexpected restart of buybacks: stock +6.3% (2024-10-17). Q3 2025, a EUR 250m programme in line with expectations and a beat: +3.5% (2025-10-16). Both dates come from the estimated-date history in the baseline.
findings.original_quote: Heinäkuun Q2-raportin yhteydessä Nordea ei julkistanut uutta omien osakkeiden takaisinosto-ohjelmaa. Johto kertoi arvioivansa voitonjakoa myöhemmin uudelleen ja priorisoivansa tällä hetkellä pääomien käyttöä kasvuun. Omat ennusteemme odottavat vielä yhtä 250 MEUR:n ohjelmaa tälle vuodelle. (Nordea announced no new buyback with Q2; management said it would reassess distribution later and currently prioritises capital use for growth. Our forecasts still expect one more EUR 250m programme this year.)
findings.why_not_priced: This is a decision the company makes in the release, so nothing has disclosed it. The thin headroom over the buffer and the growth-first language point to a risk that the expected programme is absent or smaller. If the market had priced its absence, Nordea would not be trading at a ~6% dividend-plus-buyback yield with analysts modelling 250m.
findings.independence: Nordea's own Q2 release: 'Nordea will continuously assess the opportunity to use share buy-backs as a tool to distribute excess capital' and 'we continue to deploy capital for profitable growth' (https://www.nordea.com/en/press/2026-07-16/half-year-results-2026-and-decision-on-mid-year-dividend). Buyback completion release: https://www.nordea.com/en/press/2026-04-21/nordea-completes-its-share-buy-back-programme-announced-in-december-2025

findings.finding: The ECB's rate hikes (June and September 2026) feed deposit margins in Denmark and Finland with a lag. Inderes raised its forecasts for later years because the hikes lift Nordea's NII 'more strongly from Q4'. Management commentary on the Q4 NII trajectory in the release is a likely positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed the first q/q NII rise since rates began falling, and the stock moved ~+1% (estimated date 2026-07-14/16). Nordea gives no formal NII guidance, so this line moves on commentary.
findings.original_quote: Tulevien vuosien ennusteemme sen sijaan nousivat keskuspankkien koronnostojen tukiessa Nordean korkokatemarginaalia vahvemmin Q4:stä alkaen. (Our forecasts for coming years rose as central bank rate hikes support Nordea's net interest margin more strongly from Q4 onwards.)
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. Several brokers raised targets in Sep-Oct (Citi 20.00, DB 20, ABG ~20.15, a BofA upgrade, a BNP initiation at Outperform), yet the stock is -4.9% over a month and -3.95% over 20 days at 17.0. The market is holding the near-term headwind from the pre-close call rather than the Q4 uplift. Had the uplift been priced, the stock would have tracked the peers that rose on 29 Sep and the run-up would not be negative.
findings.independence: The company itself, at the pre-close call: 'de högre styrräntorna väntas ge stöd åt räntenettot över tid ... Inlåningsmarginalerna gynnas av räntehöjningarna vilket bör synas i Danmark och Finland' (https://www.placera.se/telegram/nordea-aktien-backar-efter-analytikerkonferens-20260929)

My findings net to roughly zero, with the buyback risk as a small negative against the rate-outlook positive, so there is no tension to resolve.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the pre-close/reported-quarter finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.15, leaving only the unquantified NII residual.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move' / 'the move is in the guide': abs_move_pct went from 3.0 to 3.5, because capital return and the NII outlook are new in the release and this name's Q3 buyback days moved 6.3% and 3.5%.

The buyback finding was cut from -0.4 to -0.3 with a wider range (-3.0 to +2.0). It is an inference about a management decision on a line whose reaction history is positive, so its weight in p_up stays small.
Truncated-zero rule: positioning_check states that there is no anchor rather than that no one is short.
